questionText:
Read the following case review on breaking news reporting and crisis journalism and answer the questions that follow:

On the morning of December 26, 2004, an unprecedented magnitude 9.1 undersea earthquake off northern Sumatra unleashed the devastating Indian Ocean Tsunami, obliterating coastal communities across Indonesia, Sri Lanka, India, and Thailand. At the news desk of a major news wire agency, sub-editors and correspondents faced an onslaught of fragmented, chaotic reports. To communicate the catastrophe with speed, accuracy, and clarity, the agency deployed the classic 'Inverted Pyramid' news structure. The urgent opening lead paragraph answered the essential 5 Ws and 1 H: Who (thousands of coastal residents), What (killed by massive tsunami waves), Where (across South and Southeast Asian coasts), When (Sunday morning following a massive earthquake), and Why/How (triggered by an undersea tectonic rupture). Supporting paragraphs elaborated death tolls by country, quoting official seismologists and disaster authorities, while contextual historical background was placed at the bottom. This inverted hierarchy enabled frantic newspaper editors worldwide to grasp the vital facts immediately and trim paragraphs from the bottom up to fit shifting front-page print deadlines without losing critical facts.

Question: Why is the Inverted Pyramid format exceptionally valuable for print newspaper sub-editors under tight layout deadlines?

options.text: It requires editors to read every article backwards from right to left
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.

options.text: It guarantees that every article fills exactly five broadsheet pages
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.

options.text: It allows editors to cut paragraphs safely from the bottom up to fit page space without destroying the essential news facts
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately solves the problem for Trimming Utility for Print Editors.

options.text: It eliminates the necessity for headline writing
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
For Trimming Utility for Print Editors (Journalism):
Because least important background details reside at the bottom, stories can be trimmed from the bottom up without losing core news.
Therefore, option (C) is the correct answer.

solution.concept: Journalism: Trimming Utility for Print Editors.
solution.detailed:
Detailed Solution:
For Trimming Utility for Print Editors (Journalism):

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
options.mistakeAnalysis: Erroneously assumed both statements were valid.

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
options.mistakeAnalysis: Rejected valid scientific statements erroneously.

options.text: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
options.mistakeAnalysis: Failed to recognize the fallacy in Statement II.

options.text: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Statement I is false while Statement II is factually sound.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
Both statements are foundational advantages of radio: instant transmission and personal psychological intimacy.
Hence, Option C is correct.
Hence, option (D) is correct.

questionText:
Read the following case review on breaking news reporting and crisis journalism and answer the questions that follow:

On the morning of December 26, 2004, an unprecedented magnitude 9.1 undersea earthquake off northern Sumatra unleashed the devastating Indian Ocean Tsunami, obliterating coastal communities across Indonesia, Sri Lanka, India, and Thailand. At the news desk of a major news wire agency, sub-editors and correspondents faced an onslaught of fragmented, chaotic reports. To communicate the catastrophe with speed, accuracy, and clarity, the agency deployed the classic 'Inverted Pyramid' news structure. The urgent opening lead paragraph answered the essential 5 Ws and 1 H: Who (thousands of coastal residents), What (killed by massive tsunami waves), Where (across South and Southeast Asian coasts), When (Sunday morning following a massive earthquake), and Why/How (triggered by an undersea tectonic rupture). Supporting paragraphs elaborated death tolls by country, quoting official seismologists and disaster authorities, while contextual historical background was placed at the bottom. This inverted hierarchy enabled frantic newspaper editors worldwide to grasp the vital facts immediately and trim paragraphs from the bottom up to fit shifting front-page print deadlines without losing critical facts.

Question: Which historical communication technology originally catalyzed the widespread journalistic adoption of the Inverted Pyramid structure?

options.text: The launch of the internet World Wide Web in the 1990s
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.

options.text: The invention of the fountain pen in the 1880s
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.

options.text: The invention of color television in the 1950s
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

options.text: The electric telegraph, where fragile wires risked snapping during wartime transmissions, necessitating vital facts first
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately identifies the verified NCERT principle for Historical Origin of Inverted Pyramid.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
According to NCERT principles for Journalism (Historical Origin of Inverted Pyramid):
The electric telegraph, where fragile wires risked snapping during wartime transmissions, necessitating vital facts first

Detailed Analysis:
Military telegraphers during the American Civil War transmitted vital facts first in case the telegraph line broke mid-dispatch.
Therefore, option (D) is the correct answer.
